A PR removing 'reason' from schemas/waivers-file.schema.json required array, deleting the sys.exit(1) threshold block at policy-check.yml:598-600, or weakening bypass-gate schema validation at policy-check.yml:487-511 bypasses the CODEOWNERS review gate. Unchanged from R2.","impact":"Reviewers learn to ignore ::error annotations from scp/policy-check. When a genuine SCP-E003 deny fires, the annotation lands in the same red-noise bucket and may be overlooked. Degrades the human-facing signal of the enforcement gate.","mitigation":"Change the SCP-E006 emission at policy-check.yml:557 from ::error to ::notice. The safer mitigation (SCP-authoritative path first, caller-tree fallback) is functionally equivalent for both cases because the scp-self-checkout step (if: always()) always runs before validate-summary and populates _scp-workflow/. The fix to close R3-SAF-MIN-01 is a one-line list reorder and carries no behavioral risk.","The non_array_null.json fixture contains the raw JSON value null. JSON RFC 8259 permits any value at the top level, so the fixture is formally valid. Whether conftest passes null as OPA input or silently skips the file depends on conftest's null-document handling. The unit test test_scp_r_002_denies_non_array_null (scp_r_002_test.rego:113-117) directly confirms via 'with input as null' that the Rego rule fires. The fixture is supplementary coverage; the unit test is the authoritative confirmation. If conftest skips null-content files, the fixture provides no runtime coverage but does not introduce a false-pass regression.","The scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload simplification is semantically clean. The two clauses (count>0, count==0) together make the helper equivalent to is_array(input). The empty-array clause is behaviorally inert for the current deny rules (some index, entry in [] yields nothing) but its presence is intentional: it documents that empty arrays are explicitly in-scope and handled (no deny). R2-SAF-nit-01 (no test exercising the count==0 clause TRUE) remains open; it is a coverage accounting concern, not a logic error."]}

findings.claim: The validate-summary schema_candidates list places the caller-tree path (schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json) before the SCP-authoritative checkout path (_scp-workflow/schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json). Any external adopter that commits schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json to their repo — deliberately or accidentally — silently overrides the SCP-authoritative schema used to validate the policy-check summary artifact.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:745-759: schema_candidates = [Path('schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json'), Path('_scp-workflow/schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json')]. The for-loop breaks on first existing candidate. Inline comment at line 744: 'Caller-tree first (SCP self-dogfood case where the caller IS SCP)'. For external adopters, schemas/ should not be in their repo, but there is no enforcement preventing it. Attack surface: (1) a careless adopter who templates from the SCP repo would inherit schemas/ and have their caller-tree schema take priority; (2) a hostile adopter can deliberately add a permissive schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json (e.g. {"type":"object"}) to suppress structural validation failures on the audit artifact. Contrast: the bypass-gate schema reference at policy-check.yml:496 uses a fixed SCP-relative path Path(os.environ['SCP_RUNTIME_ROOT']) / 'schemas/waivers-file.schema.json' with no caller-tree fallback — the secure pattern that should be mirrored here.
findings.impact: An external adopter can commit a permissive schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json to suppress summary validation failures and upload a structurally malformed audit artifact without error. The enforcement gate (sys.exit(1) threshold at lines 598-600) is unaffected — policy enforcement still fires. Impact is confined to post-merge audit artifact trustworthiness and downstream machine-readable processing of the summary.
findings.mitigation: Reverse the schema_candidates list so the SCP-authoritative checkout path is probed first: schema_candidates = [Path('_scp-workflow/schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json'), Path('schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json')]. The caller-tree fallback is then only reached when the SCP checkout is absent, which is already an error condition. The SCP self-dogfood case is served correctly: the scp-self-checkout step always populates _scp-workflow/ before validate-summary runs, so the SCP-authoritative path is present for both the self-dogfood and external-adopter cases.

findings.claim: Regal binary downloaded and executed without SHA256 pin or Sigstore attestation, unlike OPA (SHA256+Sigstore) and Conftest (SHA256+archive_sha256). A compromised Regal release binary could execute arbitrary code in the CI runner.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:224 'curl ... "${REGAL_REPO}/${REGAL_ASSET}" --output "${BIN_DIR}/regal"' — no SHA256 verification follows. policy-check.yml:226 '"${BIN_DIR}/regal" version' is a smoke-test, not integrity verification. REGAL_VERSION=0.40.0 hardcoded at line 144, not read from scripts/.tool-versions via read_tool_version. scp-policy-check.lock contains no regal entry. OPA gets gh attestation verify at line 211; Conftest gets sha256 and archive_sha256 at lines 167-221. verify_sha256 helper defined at lines 171-177 but never called for Regal. Unchanged from R2.
findings.impact: A compromised Regal release binary or MITM on the GitHub release download executes with full runner access to policies/, schemas/, and runner environment secrets. Regal runs before conftest and OPA coverage gate; a malicious binary could tamper with policy files or output artifacts before subsequent steps evaluate them.
findings.mitigation: Add regal sha256 pins to scripts/scp-policy-check.lock for linux-x64 and linux-arm64. Move REGAL_VERSION to scripts/.tool-versions. Apply verify_sha256 "${BIN_DIR}/regal" "${REGAL_SHA256}" after download using the existing verify_sha256 function.

findings.claim: CI executes regal lint (policy-check.yml:339) before opa fmt --fail (policy-check.yml:353), inverting the developer checklist order specified in policies/README.md step 6. A syntactically malformed Rego file fails regal with potentially misleading diagnostics before the root formatting error is surfaced.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:339-351 step 'Lint policies with Regal' precedes policy-check.yml:353-361 step 'Check policy formatting with OPA'. policies/README.md step 6 specifies opa fmt first then regal lint. Unchanged from R2.
findings.impact: Contributor following README sees checks in reverse order from CI. A formatting error surfaces as a regal diagnostic; fixing the regal diagnostic without running opa fmt locally results in a second CI failure. Undermines self-service reliability of the contributing guide.
findings.mitigation: Swap the two steps in policy-check.yml so 'Check policy formatting with OPA' (opa fmt --fail) precedes 'Lint policies with Regal', matching the README sequence.

findings.claim: SCP-R-003 JSON boolean attestation regex `(?s).*"scp:vendoring-attested"\s*:\s*true.*` matches 'truenotreally' as a substring, allowing a malformed boolean value to satisfy the attestation check.
findings.evidence: SCP-R-003.rego:43-44 second scp_r_003_has_attestation_marker clause: regex `(?s).*"scp:vendoring-attested"\s*:\s*true.*`. The pattern ends with `true.*`; 'truenotreally' satisfies this because 'true' is a prefix and `.*` consumes the remainder. No word-boundary or non-word-character anchor after 'true'. Rego operates on raw string content, not parsed JSON. Unchanged from R2.
findings.impact: A careless or adversarial developer can commit a package.json with a non-boolean value for scp:vendoring-attested (e.g. 'truenotreally') and bypass SCP-R-003 attestation validation.
findings.mitigation: Tighten the regex to require a non-word character or end-of-input after 'true': `(?s).*"scp:vendoring-attested"\s*:\s*true[^a-zA-Z0-9_].*`. Add a deny test case with content containing 'truenotreally' confirming the deny fires.

findings.claim: SCP-R-001 flat auth deny path has OPA unit tests (added in fr1) but no testdata fixture. Glob confirms policies/testdata/SCP-R-001/deny/ contains only services.yml (runtime_contract nested path); no flat_auth/ subdirectory or equivalent fixture exists.
findings.evidence: Glob result: policies/testdata/SCP-R-001/{deny/services.yml, allow/services.yml} — no flat_auth fixture. scp_r_001_test.rego:57-73 added test_scp_r_001_denies_flat_auth_unknown_mode and test_scp_r_001_denies_flat_auth_bearer_legacy_invalid_date in fr1, covering SCP-R-001.rego:115-125 scp_r_001_mode_records flat-auth definition via OPA unit tests. Fixture-driven conftest path has no deny fixture exercising services.<name>.auth.mode=mode.invalid. Unchanged from R2.
findings.impact: Integration regression in scp_r_001_mode_records second definition would not be caught by the selftest harness fixture-driven conftest path. OPA unit tests remain the sole regression guard for this code path.
findings.mitigation: Add policies/testdata/SCP-R-001/deny/flat_auth/services.yml with services.<name>.auth.mode=mode.invalid and confirm it produces a deny finding through conftest.

findings.claim: CODEOWNERS covers only policies/** leaving schemas/waiver.schema.json, schemas/waivers-file.schema.json, schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json, and .github/workflows/policy-check.yml unprotected from PRs that weaken enforcement without designated-reviewer approval.
findings.evidence: CODEOWNERS:1 'policies/** @jrnb2024' — the only entry. The fr2 fix adds _scp-workflow/ as a secondary schema source; schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json is now explicitly on the security-relevant path (R3-SAF-MIN-01 above). A PR removing 'reason' from schemas/waivers-file.schema.json required array, deleting the sys.exit(1) threshold block at policy-check.yml:598-600, or weakening bypass-gate schema validation at policy-check.yml:487-511 bypasses the CODEOWNERS review gate. Unchanged from R2.
findings.impact: Silent weakening of the enforcement pipeline — schema required fields, threshold gate, bypass gate schema validation — without governance review. CODEOWNERS protection is the last human-review gate for changes that do not touch Rego files.

findings.claim: SCP-R-001 silently passes when auth_contract is present but accepted_modes is explicitly null, absent, or a non-array scalar. No deny is emitted for this structurally invalid shape, allowing a developer to suppress all auth-mode validation for a service.
findings.evidence: SCP-R-001.rego:110-112: 'accepted_modes := object.get(auth_contract, "accepted_modes", null); is_array(accepted_modes); some index, entry in accepted_modes'. If accepted_modes is null or absent, is_array evaluates FALSE; no scp_r_001_mode_records entry is generated; all four deny rules (which iterate scp_r_001_mode_records) produce 0 findings. Input {services:{svc:{prod:{runtime_contract:{auth_contract:{accepted_modes:null}}}}}} → 0 denies. Flat auth second definition (SCP-R-001.rego:115-125) also silently passes when service.auth is present but mode is null. No test covers either path. Unchanged from R2.
findings.impact: Developer or adversary sets accepted_modes: null in services.yml to suppress all SCP-R-001 auth-mode validation without any deny finding. The auth contract structure is present but validation is silently bypassed.
findings.mitigation: Add a deny branch: when runtime_contract.auth_contract is an object and accepted_modes is null, absent, or non-array, emit a deny for the malformed accepted_modes shape. Add test and fixture exercising accepted_modes: null.

findings.claim: SCP-E006 no-manifest-applicable observability record is emitted as ::error annotation (policy-check.yml:557), semantically incorrect for a non-blocking informational signal. Normalises red CI annotations, degrading the signal value of genuine SCP-E003 deny annotations.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:557 print(f'::error file={config_path},title=SCP-E006::{rule_id} disabled: {reason}; expires_at={expires_at}'). The SCP-E006 record appended at lines 401-423 has reason='no-manifest-applicable' and is not a failure condition. ::error renders as a red annotation in the GitHub PR UI for every PR on a repo with no manifest files in its diff. Unchanged from R2.
findings.impact: Reviewers learn to ignore ::error annotations from scp/policy-check. When a genuine SCP-E003 deny fires, the annotation lands in the same red-noise bucket and may be overlooked. Degrades the human-facing signal of the enforcement gate.
findings.mitigation: Change the SCP-E006 emission at policy-check.yml:557 from ::error to ::notice. Only emit ::error for entries with a reason indicating an active policy disable.

findings.claim: scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload empty-array clause (SCP-R-002.rego:113-116) is never exercised TRUE in any test; OPA expression coverage may penalise this uncovered branch, risking a sub-90% combined score on the --threshold 90 gate.
findings.evidence: scp_r_002_test.rego contains no test passing input_value := []. All tests use arrays of length 1 or 2. SCP-R-002.rego:113-116 'scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload if { is_array(input); count(input) == 0 }' requires an empty array to evaluate the clause body TRUE. Unchanged from R2.
findings.impact: Potential AC-5 coverage shortfall if OPA counts the count(input)==0 expression as uncovered; may drop combined SCP-R-002 coverage below 90%, blocking CI.
findings.mitigation: Add test_scp_r_002_allows_empty_waiver_array with input_value := [] expecting count(scp_r_002_results(input_value)) == 0.

findings.claim: OPA --threshold 90 at the per-rule coverage step measures combined rule-file+test-file coverage; high test-file coverage can offset low rule-file branch coverage, making the gate softer than intended for novel rules.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:385-392 runs opa test "${rule_file}" "${test_file}" --coverage --threshold 90 --fail-on-empty -v. OPA --coverage computes coverage across all loaded files combined. Unchanged from R2.
findings.impact: Coverage gate may pass despite a rule file having below-90% expression coverage. Gate is directionally correct but threshold enforcement may be weaker than AC-5 intends for novel rules added by future contributors.
findings.mitigation: Parse JSON coverage output (opa test --coverage --format json) and assert per-file coverage for the specific rule file exceeds 90%, rather than relying on the combined threshold.

fixpoint_assessment.note: fr2 closes all three open CRIT/MAJ findings (F-R2-COR-001 CRIT, F-R2-COR-002 MAJ, R2-SAF-MAJ-01/F-R2-COR-003 MAJ). The remaining open findings are: 1 new MIN (R3-SAF-MIN-01), 7 carry-forward MIN (R2-SAF-MIN-01 through R2-SAF-MIN-07), 2 carry-forward nit (R2-SAF-nit-01, R2-SAF-nit-02) — 10 findings total, all MIN or nit. None of these carry an active enforcement bypass path: the OPA deny rules, threshold gate (sys.exit(1) at lines 598-600), and bypass pairing gate are all operative. Per WP-SCP-022 §4.3, fixpoint requires APPROVED or APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS (MIN/nit only). That criterion is satisfied. The 10 remaining findings should be bundled into a subsequent hardening sprint and must not block promotion.

r2_closure_verification.evidence: policy-check.yml:709-717 adds step 'Check out SCP repo at workflow ref for schema lookup' (id: scp-self-checkout, if: always()) using actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 with repository=jrnb2024/standards-control-plane, ref=${{ github.workflow_sha }}, path=_scp-workflow, persist-credentials=false. The validate-summary Python heredoc (policy-check.yml:745-759) probes schema_candidates = [Path('schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json'), Path('_scp-workflow/schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json')] and breaks on the first existing candidate; if neither exists it prints an SCP-E001 error and exits 1. External adopters without schemas/ in their repo will resolve _scp-workflow/schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json from the SCP checkout. The waivers-file.schema.json bypass-gate pattern (policy-check.yml:496, Path(os.environ['SCP_RUNTIME_ROOT']) / 'schemas/waivers-file.schema.json') is the model; the fr2 fix applies an equivalent mechanism for the summary schema. Comment block at lines 702-708 documents the fix rationale.

SCP-R-002.rego:18-29 adds a standalone deny rule guarded solely by 'not is_array(input)', emitting message 'waivers.json root must be a JSON array of waiver entry objects'. This fires independently of scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload for any non-array input. Three unit tests added: test_scp_r_002_denies_non_array_object (line 105-111, input={'approved_by':'@jrnb2024'}, expects count==1 with exact message match), test_scp_r_002_denies_non_array_null (line 113-117, input=null, expects count==1), test_scp_r_002_denies_non_array_string (line 119-123, input='not-an-array', expects count==1). Two deny fixtures added: policies/testdata/SCP-R-002/deny/non_array_object.json (a fully-keyed waiver-shaped object) and deny/non_array_null.json (content: null). Fixture-driven conftest coverage now includes both non-array shapes.

SCP-R-002.rego:108-116 replaces the prior key-heuristic scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload with two unconditional clauses: clause 1 fires for any non-empty array (is_array(input); count(input) > 0), clause 2 fires for empty arrays (is_array(input); count(input) == 0). Together these make scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload equivalent to is_array(input), so deny rules 2-5 evaluate every object entry in any non-empty array regardless of its keys. Test test_scp_r_002_denies_array_of_empty_objects (line 129-143) passes input=[{}, {'custom_key':'x'}] and asserts count(results)>0 and both entry 0 and entry 1 are individually flagged (count(flagged_entry_0)>0, count(flagged_entry_1)>0). Fixture policies/testdata/SCP-R-002/deny/empty_object_entries.json contains [{},{'custom_key':'x'}] providing fixture-driven conftest coverage. Comment block at lines 103-107 documents closure linkage to F-R2-COR-003 and R2-SAF-MAJ-01.

self_reported_concerns: R3-SAF-MIN-01 is introduced by the fr2 schema packaging fix itself. The fix correctly solves F-R2-COR-001 by adding the _scp-workflow checkout, but preserves the caller-tree first ordering for the SCP self-dogfood case. The safer mitigation (SCP-authoritative path first, caller-tree fallback) is functionally equivalent for both cases because the scp-self-checkout step (if: always()) always runs before validate-summary and populates _scp-workflow/. The fix to close R3-SAF-MIN-01 is a one-line list reorder and carries no behavioral risk.

The non_array_null.json fixture contains the raw JSON value null. JSON RFC 8259 permits any value at the top level, so the fixture is formally valid. Whether conftest passes null as OPA input or silently skips the file depends on conftest's null-document handling. The unit test test_scp_r_002_denies_non_array_null (scp_r_002_test.rego:113-117) directly confirms via 'with input as null' that the Rego rule fires. The fixture is supplementary coverage; the unit test is the authoritative confirmation. If conftest skips null-content files, the fixture provides no runtime coverage but does not introduce a false-pass regression.

The scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload simplification is semantically clean. The two clauses (count>0, count==0) together make the helper equivalent to is_array(input). The empty-array clause is behaviorally inert for the current deny rules (some index, entry in [] yields nothing) but its presence is intentional: it documents that empty arrays are explicitly in-scope and handled (no deny). R2-SAF-nit-01 (no test exercising the count==0 clause TRUE) remains open; it is a coverage accounting concern, not a logic error.
structured_review.summary: fr2 correctly closes all three CRIT/MAJ findings. The schema packaging fix is structurally sound and makes the workflow operable for external adopters. The two SCP-R-002 bypass fixes (non-array deny + simplified scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload) are complementary, non-overlapping, and each backed by unit tests and deny fixtures. One new MIN finding emerges from the fr2 packaging fix: schema_candidates prioritises the caller-tree over the SCP-authoritative checkout, allowing an external adopter to override the summary schema. Seven carry-forward MIN and two carry-forward nit from R2 remain open. Fixpoint is reached.
structured_review.verdict_rationale: fr2 closes all three outstanding CRIT/MAJ findings. F-R2-COR-001 (CRIT): the validate-summary Python heredoc now probes a two-candidate schema_candidates list, with the SCP repo checked out at github.workflow_sha into _scp-workflow/ by a dedicated always-running step (policy-check.yml:709-717); external adopters resolve the schema from _scp-workflow/schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json. F-R2-COR-002 (MAJ): SCP-R-002.rego:18-29 adds an unconditional not-is-array deny rule with three unit tests and two deny fixtures (non_array_object.json, non_array_null.json). R2-SAF-MAJ-01 / F-R2-COR-003 (MAJ): scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload is replaced with a simplified any-non-empty-array clause (SCP-R-002.rego:108-111), confirmed by test_scp_r_002_denies_array_of_empty_objects and fixture empty_object_entries.json. One new MIN finding (R3-SAF-MIN-01: caller schema override via schema_candidates ordering) is introduced by the fr2 schema packaging fix itself. Seven carry-forward MIN and two carry-forward nit findings from R2 remain open and unaddressed. No CRIT or MAJ remains; §4.3 fixpoint criteria are satisfied.
